p: Whiteley's set-up, with shops and restaurants clustered close together, makes it easy to split a group. One grown-up can take the climbers to their session while another gets the boring errands done, then everybody meets up for lunch. Do check the age and supervision rules when you book, as climbing centres usually have guidelines on how many children each adult can look after. Trainers with a decent grip help more than you'd think on the smaller holds.

Whiteley's location between Southampton and Portsmouth puts plenty of family attractions within easy reach. Manor Farm Country Park near Botley is a working historic farm with animals, a farmhouse and old farm buildings, plus riverside walks along the Hamble. The village of Hamble-le-Rice sits at the mouth of the river, with sailing boats, a little ferry to Warsash and pubs with a view.

History lovers can explore Titchfield Abbey, a ruined abbey later turned into a Tudor mansion, now looked after by English Heritage. Royal Victoria Country Park in Netley has a huge open space beside Southampton Water, a chapel tower with views and a miniature railway on some days. For a bigger day out, Portsmouth Historic Dockyard is home to HMS Victory and the Mary Rose, while Southampton's SeaCity Museum tells the story of the city's link with the Titanic. Whiteley is just off the M27, so it's easy to fit a climb into a wider Hampshire trip, whichever direction you're heading.
